body:
## Why

Pension-Data#878 cannot safely consume the shared PDF extraction output. At Doc-Lineage main `0605500`, `src/doc_lineage/extract/pdf.py:84-91` stores only normalized text and `_normalize_reading_order()` at line 122 collapses every row into one string. `src/doc_lineage/extract/models.py:13-20` exposes no preserved line representation. A bounded Astra Medium assessment executed Pension-Data’s unchanged metric extractor and found that combining rows can change AAL $600 million into $600 billion and funded ratio 0.8 into 0.008 while still yielding all expected metrics. This is an upstream information-loss blocker, not a request to change actuarial semantics.

## Scope

Add an additive preserved-line field to PDF extraction spans for consumers that need original row and unit boundaries. Keep existing normalized `Span.text` behavior compatible. Carry the field through extraction and cache reads; ensure legacy cached native-text spans cannot hide the new data. This is the nearest bounded prerequisite for stranske/Pension-Data#878.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change normalized `Span.text`, comparison semantics, actuarial metric rules, or other repositories.
- Do not claim line boundaries recover a table schema or guarantee a downstream parser’s metric parity.
- Do not add another PDF extractor or OCR engine.
- Scaffold-only completion does not count: a field that is never populated through public `extract()` or disappears on cache reload fails this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add optional `Span.text_lines` in `src/doc_lineage/extract/models.py`, preserving source lines without changing `text`.
- [ ] Populate line data for native PDF and OCR spans in `src/doc_lineage/extract/pdf.py`; refresh old cached native spans that lack it.
- [ ] Round-trip and validate line data in `src/doc_lineage/extract/cache.py`, tolerating legacy cache data with a safe refresh.
- [ ] Add `tests/test_extract_lines.py` covering multiline metric values, horizontal separators, page attribution, OCR lines, fresh disk-cache reads, and legacy-cache refresh through public `extract()`.
- [ ] Document the additive extraction contract and its limitations in `README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python -m pytest tests/test_extract_lines.py tests/test_extract_coverage.py -q` exits 0 with nonzero collected tests; the multiline metric test returns separate original lines and the same normalized text as before. Capture command output in the PR.
- [ ] The cache tests reconstruct a fresh cache instance, return the same `text_lines`, and re-extract a legacy cached native span that lacks line data.
- [ ] The OCR case executes real PDF page rasterization with a controlled recognizer and preserves its multiline output and page number; it does not claim OCR accuracy.
- [ ] Temporarily replacing native `text_lines` with a single normalized line in `src/doc_lineage/extract/pdf.py` causes `tests/test_extract_lines.py::test_pdf_preserves_metric_lines_and_normalized_text` to FAIL; restore the code and capture the passing rerun in the PR.

## Implementation Notes

Use the existing pypdf and OCR outputs before normalization, not a new parser. Leave Pension-Data#878 pending until this API lands and its consumer adapter passes exact metric-value and provenance tests. Preserve the existing shared extraction dependency and avoid a silent legacy fallback for malformed input.
title: Preserve PDF source lines for safe metric extraction consumers
